LESSON: GENERAL ANIMAL HEALTH

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: AGRICULTURE FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Animal Production
Topic 2.3: General Animal Health
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers General Animal Health, part of Animal Production in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 AGRICULTURE FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How is animal health important in animal production? 2. How can animal diseases be prevented on the farm?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on General Animal Health together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
● Patriotism: learner demonstrates moral duty in protecting animals against ill health by practising applicable measures of

animal disease control when rearing animals in the school.

● Respect: learner displays humility when discussing with a resource person the signs of ill health and good health in

livestock animals.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Health promotion issues: learner explains why keeping animals healthy can prevent zoonotic diseases which affect

humans.

• Animal Welfare: learner proposes and carries out applicable measures that maintain animal health

Suggested Learning Resources:

• Digital devices with assistive technology

• Print materials

• Braille materials

• Animals in the immediate environment and in school

• Resource person

• Relevant materials and equipment such as antiseptics, drugs, bolus gun, hypodermic syringes and needles

Suggested Key Skills

Compare signs of ill health and normal health in livestock production.
